cooking.title: Basic Cooking
cooking.summary: Clean, safe and simple cooking skills used in canteens, homes and small hotels.

lessons.title: A clean and safe kitchen
lessons.intro: Every good kitchen job starts with cleanliness. Employers notice this first.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds before you touch food, and again after touching raw vegetables, meat, rubbish or your phone.
Tie your hair back and keep nails short. Wear a clean apron if one is given.
Keep raw food and cooked food apart. Use a separate board or plate for each.
steps.tip: Many kitchens use colour: green board for vegetables, red for meat.

steps.text: Wipe the counter with clean water and soap before and after work. Change the cloth often.
Keep the gas off when not in use. Turn pot handles inwards so nobody knocks them.

quiz.q: When should you wash your hands?
options: Only at the start of the day
Before touching food and after touching raw items or rubbish
quiz.explain: Germs are invisible. Wash before food work and after anything dirty.

quiz.q: Why turn pot handles inwards?
options: So nobody knocks the hot pot over

lessons.title: Cutting and preparing vegetables
lessons.intro: Kitchen helpers spend much of the day preparing vegetables. Speed comes later — first, safety.

steps.text: Wash vegetables in clean water. Leafy vegetables need two or three washes.
Place the board on a damp cloth so it does not slip.
Hold the vegetable with your fingertips curled inwards, like a claw. The knife touches your knuckles, never your fingertips.
Cut the vegetable flat side down so it does not roll.
Try to cut pieces the same size, so they cook evenly.
steps.tip: Ask the cook what size they want: big pieces for sabzi, small for poha or upma.

quiz.q: How should your holding hand look while cutting?
options: Holding the vegetable from the far end

quiz.q: Why cut pieces the same size?

lessons.task: At home, cut one onion and one potato into even pieces using the claw grip. Go slowly.

lessons.title: Cooking dal and rice for many people
lessons.intro: Canteens cook large amounts. The method is the same as at home, with care for measuring.

steps.text: Measure with the same cup every time. For rice, a common rule is 1 cup rice to 2 cups water.
Wash the dal until the water runs mostly clear. Soak for 20–30 minutes if time allows.
In a pressure cooker, cook dal with water, turmeric and salt — usually 3–4 whistles, then let the pressure drop by itself.
Make the tadka separately: heat oil or ghee, add jeera, then garlic or onion, then add it to the dal.
Taste before serving. Keep cooked food covered and hot, or cool it quickly and store it.

quiz.q: When is it safe to open a pressure cooker?
options: After the pressure drops by itself
When the lid is still hissing

tailoring.title: Tailoring
tailoring.summary: From threading a machine to stitching a straight seam — the base of every tailoring job.

lessons.title: Know your machine
lessons.intro: A tailoring unit will first see if you can handle a machine calmly.

steps.text: Learn the main parts: hand wheel, needle, presser foot, bobbin, thread guide and pedal.
Always turn the hand wheel towards you, never away.
Thread the machine from the spool, through each guide, down to the needle — front to back.
Wind the bobbin and place it so the thread pulls out in the right direction.
Lower the presser foot before you start stitching, and keep fingers away from the needle.
steps.tip: Practise on paper without thread to learn to sew straight lines.

quiz.q: Which way should the hand wheel turn?
What must you do before stitching?

lessons.title: Measuring correctly
lessons.intro: Good measurement saves cloth and makes customers come back.

steps.text: Use a soft measuring tape. Keep it flat, not twisted, and not too tight.
Write each measurement immediately with the customer's name.
Common measurements: chest, waist, hip, shoulder, sleeve length and full length.
Measure twice. If the two numbers differ, measure a third time.
Add seam allowance (usually 1–2 cm) when you cut the cloth, not when you measure.

quiz.q: When do you add seam allowance?

lessons.task: Measure the length and width of a pillow cover at home twice, and write both numbers.

lessons.title: Straight seams, hems and buttons
lessons.intro: Most assistant work is seams, hems and buttons. Neatness matters more than speed.

steps.text: Pin or tack two pieces of cloth together with the good sides facing each other.
Keep the cloth edge in line with the guide mark on the machine plate and sew slowly.
At the start and end, sew back 3–4 stitches to lock the seam.
For a hem, fold the edge twice, press it flat, then stitch close to the fold.
For a button, mark the spot, sew through the holes 6–8 times, then wind thread under the button to make a small stem.

quiz.q: How do you stop a seam from opening?
options: Sew a few stitches backward at start and end

repair.title: Basic Repair
repair.summary: Safe habits and first checks for fans, coolers and small appliances.

lessons.title: Safety first, always
lessons.intro: In repair work, safety is the most important skill. A good mechanic is a careful one.

steps.text: Switch off and unplug the appliance before opening it. Switching off is not enough — pull out the plug.
Never touch wires with wet hands or while standing on a wet floor. Wear rubber slippers.
Use tools with insulated (rubber or plastic) handles.
Capacitors in fans and coolers can hold charge. Let an experienced person show you how to handle them.
If you are not sure, stop and ask. It is never wrong to ask.

quiz.q: Before opening a fan, you should…
options: Switch off and pull out the plug

quiz.q: If you are unsure about a wire, you should…

lessons.title: Know your tools
lessons.intro: Using the right tool makes the job faster and keeps parts from breaking.

steps.text: Screwdrivers: flat (minus) and star (plus). Choose the size that fits the screw head fully.
Pliers grip and bend; cutters cut wire. Do not use pliers as a hammer.
A tester screwdriver lights up when a wire is live. Check it on a known live socket first.
Keep screws in a small box in the order you removed them.
Clean and return tools to their place at the end of the day.
steps.tip: Taking a photo with a phone before opening helps you put it back right.

quiz.q: Why keep screws in order?
options: To put the appliance back correctly

lessons.title: When a fan does not run
lessons.intro: Most problems are simple. Check from the easiest thing to the hardest.

steps.text: Is there power? Check the switch, plug and the socket with another device.
Does the fan hum but not turn? The capacitor may be weak — this is very common.
Does the fan turn slowly? Clean dust from the blades and check the bearings.
Is there a burning smell? Stop. The winding may be damaged — tell the senior mechanic.
Write down what you checked and what you found. Customers trust a clear explanation.

quiz.q: A fan hums but does not turn. A common cause is…

lessons.task: Look at a fan at home (switched off). Find the blades, the motor and the regulator.

gardening.title: Gardening
gardening.summary: Soil, seeds and watering — the daily work of gardens, farms and nurseries.

lessons.title: Understanding soil
lessons.intro: Healthy plants grow in healthy soil.

steps.text: Good soil is loose and crumbly, not hard like stone or sticky like clay.
Mix compost or old cow-dung manure into the soil to feed it.
Break big lumps and remove stones and plastic.
Soil should hold some water but not stay muddy. Puddles mean poor drainage.
Wear gloves or wash hands well after working with manure.

quiz.q: What improves soil?

lessons.title: Sowing seeds
lessons.intro: Each seed needs the right depth and space.

steps.text: A simple rule: sow a seed about two times as deep as its size.
Leave space between seeds so the plants do not fight for light.
Cover lightly with soil and press gently.
Water with a fine spray so seeds are not washed away.
Mark the row with the name and date of sowing.

quiz.q: How deep should a seed go?

lessons.task: Sow a few methi or dhania seeds in a small pot and note the date.

lessons.title: Watering the right way
lessons.intro: More plants die from wrong watering than from anything else.

steps.text: Water early morning or evening, not in the hot afternoon.
Water the roots, not the leaves.
Check the soil with a finger: if the top 2–3 cm are dry, it is time to water.
Too much water makes leaves turn yellow and roots rot.
In summer, a layer of dry leaves (mulch) keeps the soil moist longer.

quiz.q: Best time to water?
Yellow leaves and soft roots often mean…

digital.title: Digital Basics
digital.summary: Use a phone with confidence and stay safe from fraud.

lessons.title: Getting comfortable with a phone
lessons.intro: You do not need to know everything. A few basics take you far.

steps.text: Tap once to open. Press and hold for more options. Swipe to move between screens.
The home button or bottom line brings you back to the main screen.
Use the microphone button on the keyboard to speak instead of typing.
Save important numbers with clear names, like 'Kendra Didi' or 'Factory Office'.
Keep the phone charged and the screen locked with a PIN only you know.

quiz.q: To speak instead of type, you press…

lessons.title: UPI and money safety
lessons.intro: Digital payments are useful — and fraudsters know it. Learn the simple rules.

steps.text: You need your UPI PIN only to SEND money, never to receive it.
Never share your PIN or OTP with anyone — not even someone who says they are from the bank.
Before paying, check the name that appears on the screen.
A real employer never asks you to pay money to get a job.
steps.tip: If anyone asks for a 'registration fee' for a job, report it on KAABIL.

steps.text: If you are cheated, call 1930 (cyber crime helpline) as soon as possible.

quiz.q: To RECEIVE money, do you need your PIN?
Someone asks ₹500 to give you a job. You should…

lessons.title: Filling a simple online form
lessons.intro: Many services now ask for an online form. Take it slowly.

steps.text: Read each box label before typing. A star (*) usually means the box is required.
Type your name exactly as it is on your ID.
Mobile number: 10 digits, without 0 or +91 unless asked.
Check everything once before pressing Submit.
Take a screenshot of the confirmation page or write down the reference number.

quiz.q: After submitting a form, you should…

lessons.task: Ask a centre helper to show you a practice form and fill it with your details.

nursery.title: Nursery & Plant Care
nursery.summary: Potting, cuttings and daily care — the work of plant nurseries.

lessons.title: Filling pots and bags
lessons.intro: Nurseries fill hundreds of pots each day. Doing it right makes plants strong.

steps.text: Common potting mix: soil, sand and compost in roughly equal parts.
Make sure the pot or grow-bag has holes at the bottom for water to drain.
Fill up to about two fingers below the rim, so water does not overflow.
Tap the pot gently to settle the mix. Do not press it hard.
Line pots in straight rows. It makes watering and counting easy.

quiz.q: Why do pots need holes at the bottom?

lessons.title: Growing from cuttings
lessons.intro: Many plants like rose, money plant and hibiscus grow from a piece of stem.

steps.text: Choose a healthy stem, about the length of your hand.
Cut just below a node (the bump where a leaf grows) with a clean, sharp blade.
Remove the lower leaves and keep only 2–3 at the top.
Plant the cutting in moist mix and keep it in shade.
Keep the soil moist, not wet. New roots usually come in 2–4 weeks.

quiz.q: Where do you cut the stem?
options: In the middle of a leaf

lessons.title: Spotting plant problems
lessons.intro: A nursery worker's eyes protect the whole nursery.

steps.text: Check leaves on both sides every morning.
White powder, sticky leaves or tiny insects mean pests. Separate that plant.
Brown, dry edges can mean too little water or too much sun.
Tell the supervisor before spraying anything. Some sprays are harmful.
Always wash hands after handling sprays or fertiliser.

quiz.q: You see insects on a plant. First you…
options: Separate the plant and tell the supervisor

lessons.task: Look closely at five plants and note anything unusual on the leaves.

packaging.title: Packaging
packaging.summary: Weighing, packing and labelling — accurate, steady work in demand everywhere.

lessons.title: Weighing accurately
lessons.intro: Every packet must have the right weight. Customers and inspectors check this.

steps.text: Put the empty packet on the scale and press 'Tare' or zero.
Fill until the scale shows the target weight, for example 500 g.
If it goes over, remove a little. A few grams over is fine; under is not.
Keep the scale clean and on a flat table.
Every hour, check the scale with a known weight if one is available.

quiz.q: What does 'Tare' do?
options: Sets the scale to zero with the packet on it

lessons.title: Sealing and labelling
lessons.intro: A neat seal and a correct label make a product ready to sell.

steps.text: Remove extra air from the packet before sealing.
Seal in one straight line. Check that there are no gaps.
Stick the label straight, in the same place on every packet.
Check the date, weight and batch number on the label.
Put rejected packets in a separate box. Never mix them with good ones.

quiz.q: A packet has a gap in the seal. You…
options: Put it in the reject box

lessons.title: Packing boxes for dispatch
lessons.intro: Good packing means goods arrive safely.

steps.text: Heavy items go at the bottom, light items on top.
Fill empty spaces with paper so nothing moves.
Count the items and write the number on the box.
Tape the box in an 'H' shape across the top and bottom.
Lift with your knees bent and back straight, not by bending your back.

quiz.q: How should you lift a heavy box?

lessons.task: Pack a few household items in a box so they do not move when shaken.

sales.title: Basic Sales
sales.summary: Greeting customers, helping them choose and handling money correctly.

lessons.title: Welcoming a customer
lessons.intro: People buy from shops where they feel respected.

steps.text: Greet every customer with a smile: 'Namaste, how can I help you?'
Listen fully before you answer. Do not interrupt.
If you do not know something, say 'Let me check for you' — never guess.
Speak clearly and politely, even when the shop is busy.
Thank the customer when they leave, whether they buy or not.

quiz.q: A customer asks something you don't know. You say…

lessons.title: Helping customers choose
lessons.intro: Good sales is helping, not pushing.

steps.text: Ask simple questions: 'Which size?', 'For whom?', 'What budget?'
Show two or three options, not ten.
Tell the honest benefits and the price clearly.
If something is out of stock, suggest a similar item or when it will come.
Keep shelves neat so customers can find things themselves.

quiz.q: How many options should you usually show?

lessons.title: Handling money and bills
lessons.intro: Being careful with money builds trust with your employer.

steps.text: Say the total amount out loud to the customer.
Count the money received in front of the customer.
Count the change twice before giving it.
For UPI, wait until you see or hear the payment confirmation.
At the end of the day, match the cash with the bills.

quiz.q: For a UPI payment, when is it complete?
options: When the customer shows the phone screen with a success message or the shop speaker confirms it

lessons.task: Practise giving change: total ₹137, customer gives ₹200. How much change? (₹63)
